title: Wittmann wins from pole as Spengler's option-tyre charge reaches the Hungaroring podium
dek: Marco Wittmann led from pole to win the Hungaroring round for BMW by 6.615 seconds from Miguel Molina, while Bruno Spengler recovered from ninth on the grid to third.

chapters.title: Back in Hungary after 26 years
text: The third round of the 2014 DTM season took the series to the Hungaroring, its first race at the circuit since 1988. The narrow, twisty track near Budapest is known as a place where overtaking is difficult, and with Hankook supplying both a prime and a faster option compound, the afternoon looked certain to be decided as much by tyre strategy as by outright pace.

Mike Rockenfeller arrived as championship leader with 30 points, five clear of Marco Wittmann and Christian Vietoris, who were level on 25. Mattias Ekström had 18, Adrien Tambay 16 and Edoardo Mortara 15. The table reflected two very different races: Wittmann had won the season opener at Hockenheim, while Vietoris had taken Mercedes-AMG to victory at Oschersleben two weeks earlier after starting 16th in a wet and unpredictable race.

Audi's Miguel Molina came to Hungary hoping to turn his speed into a result after an unlucky start to the year, and Audi had a particular audience in mind: a large group of employees from its plant in Győr was due at the track. Mercedes, whose Oschersleben win had come in the rain, was looking for progress in the dry.

chapters.title: Wittmann fastest in all three segments
text: Wittmann was untouchable on Saturday. The BMW Team RMG driver topped Q1, Q2 and Q3 and took pole with a 1:36.518, 0.213 seconds clear of Timo Glock in the second MTEK BMW. Sand blowing across the track kept the grip level changing throughout the day, which made the clean laps harder to string together.

Molina, fastest in the morning practice session, was best of the Audis in third on 1:36.757, only 0.026 seconds from the front row. He had used just one set of tyres in Q1 to save a set for the final segment. Maxime Martin, in his first Q3, was fourth on 1:36.777 and António Félix da Costa fifth, so BMW had five of the first six places and six of the top ten, with Augusto Farfus sixth and Bruno Spengler ninth.

Tambay was seventh despite a spin in Q1, and Nico Müller reached Q3 to qualify eighth. Jamie Green was tenth, Mattias Ekström 11th and Mortara 12th. Rockenfeller, the championship leader, could manage only 13th, with Joey Hand 14th and Timo Scheider 15th.

It was another difficult day for Mercedes. Pascal Wehrlein, 16th, and Robert Wickens, 17th, were the only ones to escape Q1, and the five cars eliminated there were all Mercedes: di Resta, Juncadella, Paffett, Petrov and Vietoris occupied 19th to 23rd. Wehrlein said that in normal conditions points would be out of reach.

chapters.title: Wittmann gets away, Paffett is out on lap one
text: Wittmann won the start and used the opening laps to pull clear of the DRS window, so that the cars behind could not use the overtaking aid against him. Behind him the order shuffled at once. Molina made a poor start and dropped places, but recovered quickly, and within the first third of the race he had worked his way past several cars, including a tight and slightly scrappy move on Glock, to take second.

The opening corners also cost Gary Paffett his race. Contact at the start left his Mercedes damaged and he was out after a single lap. Robert Wickens, meanwhile, had a good start from 17th and ran a long, lonely race as high as seventh, while Timo Scheider's day ended after 10 laps in the Phoenix Audi.

The compounds quickly split the field. Most of the leaders started on the faster option tyre, but Spengler, from ninth, and Martin began on the harder primes and were passed by cars that were swiftly gaining ground, leaving Spengler for a time in the back of the midfield.

chapters.title: Options for the last stint, and contact in the midfield
text: The mandatory stops turned the race over. Wittmann's stop was flawless, and on the primes he was able to hold his lead over the second-placed car. For the drivers who had started on the harder tyre the story was different: Spengler, who had lost a great deal of time on the harder tyre, now fitted the option and began carving through the field, with Martin and Tambay on the same strategy a few places further back.

Glock, who had run fifth for long periods, met trouble after his stop. Mortara, on primes, tangled with him more than once, and Glock complained afterwards that he had been hit twice and forced wide. Mortara admitted that he was not proud of the fight. When the option-tyre runners arrived the BMW was swallowed up by a succession of Audis, and the race that had promised a podium turned into a fight just to stay in the points.

chapters.title: Wittmann by 6.615 seconds, Spengler rises to third
text: Wittmann took the flag after 41 laps in 1:08:35.291, 6.615 seconds ahead of Molina. He said he never felt the result was safe, since cars on options could still close up in the final laps, but his advantage was enough. Spengler completed his comeback from ninth on the grid to take third, 21.842 seconds behind the winner.

Behind him the fight for fourth was close. Mortara held fourth on the harder tyres, 29.960 seconds from the winner, with Tambay and Martin within half a second of him in fifth and sixth. Green was seventh, Félix da Costa eighth and Ekström ninth, with Rockenfeller taking the final point in tenth. Martin and Félix da Costa both scored for the first time in the DTM.

Wickens finished 11th from 17th on the grid, the best of the Mercedes drivers, who again scored no points. Müller, 12th, set the fastest lap, a 1:37.556 on lap 26. Glock came home 19th, Farfus was classified 21st, ten laps down, and Vietoris was 20th, five laps behind.

chapters.title: Wittmann takes the lead of the championship
text: Wittmann said afterwards that the strategy had worked, that he had built up a big advantage and then protected it without mistakes, and that he was not thinking about the title. The win was his second of 2014, and with 50 points he went into his home race at the Norisring as championship leader, 19 clear of Rockenfeller, who recovered a point from tenth place to reach 31. Mortara was third on 27, ahead of Tambay and Molina on 26 each and Vietoris on 25.

BMW Motorsport director Jens Marquardt praised the way Wittmann handled the pressure and said the weekend had been a pleasure to watch, while team principal Stefan Reinhold described two wins in three races as hard to believe. Spengler said it was a fantastic feeling to be back on the podium, and that ploughing through the field on options had been great fun. His team principal Charly Lamm called the podium the team's first of the year and Spengler sensational on the option tyres.

For Audi the weekend was a mixed one. Molina's second place was his reward after two unlucky rounds, and he said he now wanted to win a race. Audi's head of DTM Dieter Gass called him the only driver who could have threatened Wittmann, but admitted that qualifying had not been good enough. Audi had still not won in 2014, and Gass said the team wanted to put that right at the Norisring.

Mercedes left Hungary without a point. Wickens, the best-placed driver in 11th, said the car felt better and that the team had made a step forward, and Mercedes DTM chief Wolfgang Schattling said he expected the Norisring to suit the cars better. BMW's Glock was left angry with Mortara, while the Audi driver conceded that the fight had been hard. The next round, on 27 to 29 June, was the Norisring in Nuremberg, the street circuit on which Wittmann would race in front of his home fans.

facts.v: Wittmann won after 41 laps in 1:08:35.291, 6.615 seconds ahead of Molina.
